To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
systems analysis of circulating leukocytes can be used to diagnose sepsis, determine the pathogen responsible, and monitor immune recovery.

1) the immune response can be mapped in a cell-type specific manner in mouse models of sepsis, 2) the immune response to endotoxin in human volunteers is also cell-type specific, 3) a similar approach can be used to follow sepsis patients and determine their immune recovery, and 4), immune cartography has the potential to rapidly diagnose sepsis and identify pathogens.

1) the transcriptional activity in circulating immune effector populations can be used to discriminate between sterile inflammation and infectious etiologic agents, 2) the host response to infection can be mapped in a quantitative, reproducible manner, and 3) the host response can be used to follow the recovery of septic patients and identify patients who are not responding to therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel diagnostics and prognostics for sepsis and other complex diseases.
the development of a rapid, inexpensive and accurate blood diagnostic for the identification and treatment of sepsis.
the development of novel diagnostic and prognostic tests for the critically ill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immune cartography is a powerful tool for understanding the pathogenesis of sepsis and for developing novel therapies.
the host response to infection can be used to diagnose and monitor the course of disease.
the immune cartography approach has the potential to provide rapid diagnosis, pathogen identification, and prognostic information in sepsis and critical illness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system is a powerful, yet poorly understood, tool for the diagnosis and treatment of infectious and non-infectious diseases.
systems biology can be used to simplify the complex disease of sepsis.
we have demonstrated that systems analysis of circulating leukocytes is a promising approach to the rapid and accurate diagnosis of sepsis and other inflammatory diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host response to infection and inflammation is a complex system, but the complexity of the host response to a pathogen is not random.
systems biology is a powerful tool for identifying the commonalities in complex diseases, such as sepsis, and can be used to simplify complex disease.
the host response to sepsis can be mapped in a manner that can be used to diagnose and track the response to infection and inflammation.
